title: fire_tick is captured but never asserted — the claimed 'fire lands after crisis resolves' ordering is not pinned
detail: The test comment promises the fire lands after the crisis resolves, but fire_tick is written and never read; no resolve tick is captured and no ordering assertion exists. The E15 headline contract is only half-tested.
recommended_fix: Capture the resolve tick and assert fire_tick > resolve_tick, or delete fire_tick and drop the ordering claim from the comment.

title: balance.json wholesale reformat buries the one-block addition and drops the trailing newline
evidence:
-  "logic_hz": 20,
-  "max_ticks": 100000,
+ "logic_hz": 20,
+ "max_ticks": 100000,
...
+}
\ No newline at end of file
detail: Adding the `advance` block rewrote the entire file (2-space to 1-space indent, unicode escaped to \uXXXX, no trailing newline). Any accidental semantic drift is unreviewable in the noise and every future blame is polluted.
recommended_fix: Regenerate the diff as a minimal hand edit: insert only the `advance` block into the existing formatting and restore the trailing newline.

title: zero-demand test builds a full fixture then destroys it; claims a .Sla block but never asserts the reason
evidence:
+	// window measures nothing — the SLA term is NOT met (a vacuous pass would
+	// let an idle network advance). The gate stays blocked (.Sla), never fires.
...
+	gate_fixture(&s, cat) // topology only — the director spawns NOTHING (no demand)
...
+	run_destroy(&s)
+	run_init(&s, 1, cat.hash, TEST_LOGIC_HZ)
...
+	testing.expect_value(t, fires, 0)
detail: gate_fixture draws pipes that are immediately thrown away by run_destroy/re-init (dead work with a rambling comment), and the header asserts the gate 'stays blocked (.Sla)' while the body only checks fires == 0.
recommended_fix: Drop the first run_init/gate_fixture and assert the emitted block reason is .Sla (or no event), matching the comment.

title: SLA-block test comment claims a 6/tick sustained flood; code seeds once per tick and stops at tick 400
detail: Comment says 6/tick; the loop calls flow_seed_demand once per tick and only through tick 400 of a 700-tick run. The PR body's '~55% windowed ratio' claim is not derivable from the code as written.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment to the actual seed rate/duration, or seed the claimed rate so the windowed-ratio rationale is checkable.

title: tag-14 event payload writer added with no corresponding read-side change anywhere in the diff
detail: serialize.odin's hunk touches only the payload writer. If any code path parses event payloads back from the log, a tag-14 event will misparse or desync the stream; no reader update appears in the diff.
recommended_fix: Confirm event payloads are write-only, or add the symmetric reader branch for tag 14 (and a round-trip test).
